Referred to the House Committee on Foreign Affairs.

dimensions.assessment: Affects U.S. exporters, domestic manufacturers, technology companies, and federal export control administrators.
dimensions.evidence: long license delays at the Bureau of Industry and Security of the Department of Commerce create uncertainty for United States exporters and domestic manufacturers

dimensions.assessment: Imposes mandatory decision timelines, status notifications, quarterly reporting, and a GAO audit.
dimensions.evidence: the Secretary should make a licensing decision and notify the applicant... not later than 120 days... notify the applicant of the status

dimensions.assessment: Requires administrative tracking, quarterly reporting, and a GAO audit without specifying direct federal appropriations.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Comptroller General of the United States shall commence an audit

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 to add statutory licensing timelines, review procedures, and reporting mandates.
dimensions.evidence: Section 1756 of the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 (50 U.S.C. 4815) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory requirements for export license processing and ongoing quarterly reporting.
dimensions.evidence: not less frequently than quarterly thereafter, the Secretary shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report

missing_information: Specific administrative cost estimates for carrying out the audits and reporting
importance_detail.rationale: Establishes a 90-day decision timeline and 120-day notification requirement for the Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security regarding export license applications, along with periodic reporting and a GAO audit.
